hook_text: Bees, stop signs and Ndebele houses have something in common. Can you spot it?
clip_script: A walk in Mpumalanga. In the garden: a leaf with one line of symmetry down the middle, a butterfly the same, a flower with 5 petals and 5 lines. The beehive: hexagons, fitting with no gaps, a tessellation. In town: buildings are rectangular prisms, the water tank a cylinder, the stop sign a regular octagon with 8 lines of symmetry. And the painted Ndebele house: bold black lines, bright triangles and rectangles, and a line of symmetry right through the doorway. Nature, town and heritage, all speaking the language of shapes. Name the shapes, the lines, the repeats and the symmetry.
visual_style: Whiteboard sketches of a leaf, a honeycomb, a stop sign and an Ndebele house front, each with dotted lines of symmetry drawn in.
mood: Curious and proud, a guided walk.
pacing: Garden, town, heritage, then the four things to name.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch three patterns you find on your way home.
